sum: Ford Motor Company (F) shares rose 4.07% to $11.63 on Monday, up 45 cents, after the Dearborn, Michigan-based automaker said its Industrial Platform LLC subsidiary had agreed to acquire a minority stake in U.S. defense contractor Revolution Space, pushing the company into satellite and spacecraft manufacturing.

The stock recovered from an early low near $11.30 to trade as high as roughly $11.67 intraday. Financial terms were not disclosed, and the transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

Under the agreement, Ford will supply engineering, design, production and supply-chain resources to help the Boston-based startup scale output of next-generation spacecraft and propulsion systems. The two companies aim to move spacecraft assembly away from labor-intensive, hand-built processes toward more automated, repeatable manufacturing.
Revolution Space builds systems for missions spanning very low Earth orbit, geosynchronous altitudes and cislunar space, serving both government and commercial programs.
"Ford's strength is building complex products in large volumes, something today's growing satellite market requires," said Marin Gjaja, Ford's chief strategy officer.

Revolution Space chairman Daniel S. Goldin said the alliance would help industrialize the company's systems to meet performance requirements across a wide range of missions. Goldin is a former NASA administrator.

The companies cited World Economic Forum estimates that the global space economy could roughly triple from about $600 billion to $1.8 trillion by 2035, driven by demand for communications, navigation and Earth observation services. Satellite manufacturing alone, valued by Future Market Insights at roughly $22 billion to $26 billion in 2025, is projected to reach $87 billion to $114 billion over the next decade.

Mark Hamill Shares Rare Update On Harrison Ford Friendship Ahead Of 'Star Wars' 50th Anniversary
sum: Actors Mark Hamill and Harrison Ford have known each other for almost five decades, as 2027 marks the fiftieth anniversary of “Star Wars.” The first film, titled “A New Hope,” was released in 1977 and was followed by 1980’s “The Empire Strikes Back,” and 1983’s “Return of the Jedi.”

Unfortunately for fans, they did not share any scenes together during the sequel trilogy, which started with 2015’s “The Force Awakens” and featured the death of Ford’s character, Han Solo, at the hands of his on-screen son Kylo Ren/Ben Solo, played by Adam Driver. Kylo Ren also contributed to the death of Hamill’s character, Jedi Luke Skywalker, in 2017’s “The Last Jedi.”
Although both deaths were considered controversial, the sequel trilogy’s poor reception hasn’t affected how Hamill feels about Ford as “A New Hope” prepares to celebrate its fiftieth birthday.
Mark Hamill Reveals How Harrison Ford Impressed Him Almost Fifty Years Ago

Mark Hamill reveals that he immediately looked up to Ford when they met on the set of “A New Hope” about fifty years ago because the actor could see the entire story and wasn’t just focused on his character.

“What I was amazed [by] was not only did he have a good sense of who he was in the screenplay, he had knowledge of everything about the entire screenplay,” he recalled. “Not just his part, everybody’s part.”

“So a lot of times George is not really an actor’s director; he doesn’t want to hear about motivation or backstory,” he continued, revealing that he often went to Ford for advice. “So a lot of times I’d be talking with Harrison about it, [so] as not to bother George.”

Ford Yields 5.27%, but These 3 Auto Dividends Come With Different Risks
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Detroit and Tokyo both send their shareholders real cash. Ford Motor (NYSE:F | F Price Prediction), Toyota Motor (NYSE:TM), and Honda Motor (NYSE:HMC) have all paid dividends this year while paying for electric vehicles and absorbing tariffs. Ford leads the group with a yield of about 5.27% at today’s price. The question for income investors is whether each payout is supported by cash or only by hope. Dividend safety differs across the three, and Ford’s check is the biggest.

Ford pays a regular quarterly dividend of $0.15 per share, or $0.60 per share a year. At a share price of $11.38, that works out to a 5.27% yield. That is a high-yield payout. It falls short of the 6% bar for ultra-high-yield. Part of the yield comes from a weak share price: the stock is down 9.2% year to date.

Dividend safety: Trailing earnings are weak right now. Trailing GAAP EPS is -$1.98, dragged down by special charges, including $4.2B[1] of pre-tax charges in the second quarter. Adjusted EPS of $0.49[2] in the third quarter covered that quarter’s $0.15 dividend more than three times, and the stock trades at a forward P/E of 6. Cash flow is the real support. Through the first nine months of the year, free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) came to roughly $4.045B, compared with $1.804B in dividends paid. In 2025, Ford produced $12.467B of free cash flow and paid out $2.989B in dividends. Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance of $6B to $7B[2].

Balance sheet: Ford ended the quarter with $22.275B[2] in cash and equivalents. Consolidated debt/equity of 4.66 looks heavy, but that figure includes Ford Credit’s lending book, and the reported data doesn’t break out debt for the auto business alone. Ford Credit is pulling its weight: its pre-tax earnings rose 27% to $803M[2]. Consolidated interest coverage is a thin 2.02.
Track record: Ford suspended its dividend after the 2020-01-29 ex-dividend date and resumed it, supported by the 2021-11-18 payment. The regular $0.15 has held steady since the second half of 2022.

Weeks after he went viral for introducing his second wife to his congregation at LifeWorks Church in Ohio, Ford shared two Facebook posts pushing plural marriage, including one celebrating a married woman who says she brought the idea to her husband and her best friend.

Days before that, Ford reposted a video from a Facebook page called Black Polygamy and added the caption “That Part!!!” The page originally shared the video on November 4 with a post asking whether polygamy is a sin. The video includes a graphic listing men from the Bible and how many wives each had, from Abraham and his two wives to Solomon and his 700.

For Pastor Israel Ford, it is the latest move in a campaign that started from the pulpit. On October 25, during Sunday service at LifeWorks Church, his first wife took the microphone. Ford founded the church with her, Pastor Lydia Ford, in 2009. Lydia introduced the congregation to “Prophet’s wife and my sister in marriage, Minister Shakayla.” The church refers to Ford as a prophet. FIA shares latest ADUO results after third analysis of the 2026 F1 season
sum: "For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers," the motorsport federation announced today, following the latest analysis period covering Races 12 to 18.

Nikolas Tombazis, the federation's single-seater director said: "The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached.

"The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the Power Unit Manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons."
ADUO stands for ‘Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities’ for power unit manufacturers. It measures the performance of a PU's internal combustion engine.

If a manufacturer falls behind the benchmark engine by 2%, it receives an additional homologation opportunity for the 2026 season and one for 2027. If the deficit reaches 4%, it receives two additional homologation opportunities for each season.

After the first period, Mercedes fell within the first category, while Ferrari, Audi and Honda were in the second category, granting every manufacturer bar Red Bull Ford the opportunity to make upgrades.

The Volkswagen T7 Transporter Is Better Than Expected
sum: Volkswagen has come out guns blazing with the new Transporter T7, and if you ask me, it’s a bold and daring move. Why daring? Well, remember the collaboration between VW and Ford that gave us the Amarok and Ranger twins? The same partnership has been extended to the Transporter, which now shares its underpinnings with the Ford Tourneo Custom.

While the previous Transporter carried that distinct VW flair, this new model wears its Volkswagen badge proudly, even though, underneath, it’s very much a Ford at heart. But that’s not necessarily a bad thing — far from it.

Over our 800km journey from Johannesburg to Hoedspruit in Limpopo, the Transporter proved itself a refined, stable cruiser. It handled long stretches with ease and composure. The only real gripe was the rear seats — not the most comfortable for passengers on long hauls, and they made my attempts at a power nap rather unsuccessful. No beauty rest for me this time.

Now, onto the good stuff. The Transporter T7 has grown. It now measures 5,050mm in length, 146mm longer than before, and boasts a 3,100mm wheelbase, 97mm longer than the outgoing T6.1. The result is noticeably more space inside — ideal for families or larger groups who’ll appreciate the full seven-seat layout.

Design-wise, VW has stepped up. The new Transporter looks sleeker and more modern, with cleaner lines, smoother finishes, and a striking front end featuring contemporary LED headlight clusters. There’s also a fresh palette of exterior colours to choose from.

Inside, the cabin impresses with its premium touches. Our test model — the Life trim — was well equipped, with leather seats, a crisp 12-inch infotainment display, and an intuitive interface, even for those without a tech-savvy background. Naturally, it offers seamless connectivity via wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Other highlights include multi-zone air conditioning with physical buttons (a small but appreciated detail), keyless start, and rain-sensing wipers — which proved very handy during a downpour in Dullstroom. The multifunction steering wheel provides easy access to key controls, and both front seats feature dual armrests, adding a touch of van life comfort.

sum: BASF picked up a pair of SPE Automotive Innovation honours this week for plastic components developed with carmaking partners, though the recognition did nothing to shield the chemicals group's stock from a broad market downdraft. The shares shed 2.9% on Friday as a global retreat from AI and semiconductor names rippled through German equities, with no link established between the decline and the award announcements.

The Ludwigshafen-based company, working alongside Stellantis and L&L Products, took the SPE Automotive Innovation Award in the Chassis/Hardware category for a composite tunnel reinforcement used in the 2027 model-year Jeep Grand Cherokee. A second project earned the top prize: BASF, Toyota and Vuteq claimed the SPE Automotive Innovation Grand Award for the thermoplastic truck bed of the 2026 Toyota Tacoma, an application that also won in the Body Exterior category.

A third accolade went to BASF with Ford and Supavut Thailand in the Materials category, recognising door-handle trim on the 2026 Ford Everest. Together the three projects span different partners and vehicle applications, underscoring the group's reach across automotive supply chains.

The stock weakness had little to do with any of that. According to the Tagesschau, the worldwide selloff in AI and chip stocks weighed on the German market as a whole, and BASF was among the weakest performers in European chemicals during morning trading, dpa-AFX reported. Worries about the future momentum of AI investment drove selling pressure across sectors rather than any fresh operating news from BASF itself.

On the operating front, the picture is brighter. Roughly two weeks ago the group lifted its full-year 2026 forecast, now projecting EBITDA before special items of EUR 7.4bn to EUR 7.8bn, up from a previous range of EUR 6.9bn to EUR 7.7bn.
Third-quarter figures released on 28 October showed sales climbing 14% year on year to EUR 16.4bn, while EBITDA before special items rose 15% to EUR 1.6bn.

Beyond automotive and core chemicals, BASF has been rolling out new applications. On 30 October its trinamiX subsidiary and Eurofins Agro Testing unveiled a joint approach to mobile feed analysis for EuroTier 2026, combining NIR spectroscopy with calibration models.

Will Ford's Gen-1 Cost Reductions Drive Further Model e Improvements?
sum: Ford's F efforts to improve the profitability of its electric vehicle (EV) business are beginning to yield results, with lower losses on its first-generation (Gen-1) products supporting a gradual recovery in Model e.

In the third quarter of 2026, the segment incurred an EBIT loss of $1.06 billion, narrowing 25% from $1.41 billion in the prior-year quarter. The improvement came despite a 31% decline in revenue to $1.22 billion, reflecting lower wholesale volumes and unfavorable product mix. Ford's focus on rightsizing Gen-1 production, reducing structural costs and improving pricing is helping contain losses as it transitions toward its next-generation EV portfolio.

Ford's ongoing efforts to align production with market demand and reduce the cost base of its first-generation EV portfolio are driving progress. During the third quarter, Model e wholesale volumes declined 31% year over year to 34,000 units, primarily due to the discontinuation of the F-150 Lightning and production adjustments for the Mustang Mach-E.

However, lower Gen-1 product losses and favorable net pricing helped improve EBIT by $352 million year over year. Management also highlighted that Mustang Mach-E recorded its lowest spending level since 2023, reflecting tighter cost controls and disciplined production management.

Ford remains on track to improve Gen-1 EBIT by approximately 40% year over year in 2026. This reflects its strategy of balancing production and pricing with underlying market demand while realizing savings from a rightsized manufacturing footprint. Although continued cost reductions should support progress, achieving its 2029 Model e breakeven target will depend on disciplined spending and successful execution of its next-generation EV strategy.

Ford's efforts to narrow EV losses reflect a broader industry shift toward improving EV economics through cost reductions and production adjustments. General MotorsGM is following a similar path. During the third quarter of 2026, General Motors' EV-related net realizable value inventory adjustments declined by $400 million year over year, while EV strategic realignment charges fell to $238 million from $1.59 billion in the prior-year quarter.

Ford Shares Rise as Automaker Rejects Transportation Chief's China Criticism
sum: Ford Motor Company (F) shares climbed Thursday after the Detroit automaker issued a forceful rebuttal to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who had accused the company of deepening its dependence on Chinese technology and manufacturing at the expense of American workers.

The dispute centers on Ford's BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, a facility in Marshall that produces batteries using technology licensed from Contemporary Amperex Technology Co (CATL), the world's largest battery maker. Duffy, in a letter to Ford CEO Jim Farley, said his department was "deeply alarmed" by the arrangement and warned that Ford's strategic decisions were helping Chinese state-backed enterprises gain ground in Western markets.

Ford did not hold back in its response. The company called Duffy's letter "a wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines at the expense of a company that has done more for American manufacturing than virtually any other in the nation's history." It insisted the CATL deal is a limited technology licensing and services agreement, not a joint venture or foreign-owned manufacturing operation. Ford owns the plant, controls its operations, and employs its entire workforce.

The automaker also said Duffy's letter contained factual errors, including the characterization of its arrangement with CATL. "Ford has not proposed a joint-venture framework as described in the letter," the company stated.

Duffy's criticism extended beyond Michigan. He pointed to Ford's reported partnership with Chinese automaker Geely Auto in Spain and the company's decision to delay reshoring some Lincoln production until 2030. The secretary argued these moves deepen Ford's reliance on China and called on the company to prioritize U.S. manufacturing and technological self-reliance.
Ford pushed back on the Lincoln claims as well, saying it plans to increase U.S. production for the luxury brand.

The White House appeared to offer a counter-narrative. Its @RapidResponse47 account said Wednesday that Ford has increased U.S. investment and brought production back to the country. The administration also highlighted Ford's $3 billion investment in the Marshall battery plant, which is expected to create about 1,700 jobs.

sum: CNBC's Jim Cramer said Ford's new battery storage business gives the automaker a credible way to benefit from one of the market's hottest trends: the rapid buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
"I love what Ford is doing with this battery business," the "Mad Money" host said Wednesday.

Last month, Ford formally launched Ford Energy, a subsidiary focused on supplying large-scale battery storage systems for data centers and the electric grid. Investors initially embraced the move, sending Ford shares to a multi-year high above $17, from below $14 before the announcement. The stock has since retreated to around $14 as of Wednesday's close.

"I didn't want to recommend the stock when it was screaming higher last month in response to the news, but now that it's drifted back down to $13.96, that's a different story," Cramer said. "If you believe oil and interest rates are coming down, then you've got my blessing to buy Ford Motor."

Cramer said the opportunity comes as demand for battery storage accelerates alongside the construction of new AI data centers. At the same time, he noted that renewable energy projects also depend on storage systems to supply electricity when solar and wind generation falls short.
"We know that demand for these big backup batteries is growing like crazy because all the new data centers really can't afford to go offline," he said.
Ford plans to produce at least 20 gigawatts of battery storage capacity annually, with its first customer deliveries expected in late 2027.

sum: U.S. legacy automaker Ford F kicked off 2026 on a weak footing, and the numbers tell a clear story. The legacy automaker reported first-quarter deliveries of 457,315 vehicles, down 9% year over year. That decline reflects a broader slowdown across the auto industry as economic uncertainty, affordability concerns, elevated vehicle prices and high borrowing costs weigh on demand. Ford's arch rival General Motors GM and Japan's auto biggie Honda HMC also saw their U.S. deliveries fall around 10% and 4%, respectively.

Ford's challenges were particularly visible across key segments. Its electric vehicle (EV) business took a sharp hit, with sales plunging nearly 70% year over year to just 6,860 units, following the withdrawal of federal tax incentives and persistently high EV price tags. Meanwhile, its crown jewel — the F-Series trucks — saw volumes drop 16% to 159,901 units. Management partly attributed this to production disruptions linked to last year's aluminum plant fires, which constrained supply. Even hybrids, which had been a strong growth driver, saw sales fall nearly 20%. With the average new vehicle price hovering near $50,000 and financing costs still elevated, affordability remains a key headwind.

With Ford shares down 12% year to date, the market is clearly factoring in near-term headwinds. But the key question now is— does this represent a buy on dip opportunity, or is it better to stay on the sidelines, or even exit? Let's take a closer look.

Ford is dealing with a series of operational and cost pressures that could keep near-term performance under strain. A key issue is the supply disruption caused by a fire at a Novelis aluminum plant. The impact already led to roughly $2 billion in losses last year, with another $1 billion expected this year. On top of that, Ford may incur $1.5–$2 billion in additional costs as it sources aluminum from alternative suppliers, adding further pressure on margins.

The company is also in the middle of reshaping its EV strategy, which isn't coming cheap. It expects about $7 billion in special charges over the next two years, largely tied to strategy shifts and asset sales, with most of the cash impact likely in 2026.
